summary: Mistral introduces Robostral Navigate, an 8B in-house model that uses a single RGB camera (no LiDAR or depth sensors) to autonomously navigate robots, achieving state-of-the-art results on the R2R-CE benchmark.

mechanisms.reason: An 8B model designed to run directly on wheeled, legged and flying robots using a single camera shifts inference workloads onto embedded edge devices rather than datacentre GPUs.
mechanisms.quote: Runs on wheeled, legged, and flying robots, and generalizes across robot sizes

mechanisms.reason: The document describes a first demonstration that single-camera navigation can outperform multi-sensor (LiDAR/depth/multi-camera) systems on a held-out benchmark, a step change for the specific task class of embodied navigation.
mechanisms.quote: it beats the best single-camera approach by 9.7 points and the best system using depth or multiple cameras by 4.5 points, despite using neither

practices.reason: A team building vision-driven autonomous or robotic agents could evaluate this model's single-camera navigation and pointing-based control for their own embodied use cases.
practices.quote: It's an 8B model that takes RGB images and a plain-language instruction and moves a robot through an environment

practices.reason: The stated R2R-CE metrics (success rate, oracle success rate, SPL, navigation error) give a transferable measurement standard for teams assessing navigation models.
practices.quote: achieves 76.6% on R2R-CE (Room-to-Room in Continuous Environments) validation unseen, the benchmark for following instructions in environments held out of training
